title: The pre-commit gate counts an on-demand prose discipline as enforced
body:
**What.** In a project that declares a prose discipline (`author` or `content`), the pre-commit gate counts that discipline as enforced. It prints, eg, "intent critic gate: 1 of 1 declared language(s) enforced (content), ...". But `intent critic content --staged` is an on-demand no-op: it prints nothing, exits 0 and checks nothing. So the line says that a check ran that did not run. Intent's own commits show the same thing, because Intent declares `author` and `content`.

**Where.** `lib/templates/hooks/pre-commit.sh`:
- the dispatch loop, where `case "$rc" in 0|1|3) CHECKED+=("$lang")` puts the no-op's exit 0 into CHECKED;
- the count line, "intent critic gate: ${#CHECKED[@]} of ${#LANGS[@]} declared language(s) enforced (...)".

**Cost.** A reader of the gate's line believes that the commit's prose was checked.

**Fix.** Count an on-demand discipline on its own, eg "0 of 1 declared language(s) enforced; on demand: content (critic-prose)" (the reporter's suggestion). The gate keeps no language list of its own: `intent critic --languages` already lists each language that has a headless code critic, so the gate can take the on-demand set from that answer.

**Reported.** 2026-11-25, by a client estate's supervisor on hv's word, against Intent 3.5.3 from Homebrew. Severity low.

Resolution: Fixed at bfc1b908b, where the pre-commit gate counts an on-demand prose discipline apart from the enforced languages, and at de4f3dd7b, where the shipped hook cites nothing of Intent's own tracker. Shipped in v3.5.4.
